newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Arabs freed in policewoman 'rape' case.
newsitem.headline: French Arabs freed in policewoman 'rape' case.

text.p: A court on Friday released on bail two French-Arab youths for lack of evidence in an alleged gang rape of an off-duty policewoman.
The case outraged police until it emerged their colleague had claimed falsely on an earlier occasion to have been raped.
The court ruled that Djamel Eddouibi, 19, and another youth, who cannot be named because he is under 18, could be released on bail since there was no "immediate further cause to detain them."
The two remain officially under judicial investigation, together with two others released earlier, pending a decision on whether charges will stand or be dropped, according to judicial sources.

Clashes are frequent between police and delinquent youths in sprawling high-rise immigrant suburbs of Paris and the rape case was seized upon by some police unions and xenophobic rightist groups when it became public last October.

The policewoman, 28, had failed to show up for work for several days when she reported that four youths -- three Arabs and a black, all French nationals -- had beaten and raped her on a late-night commuter train four days before.
Because of the time lapse, doctors were unable to ascertain rape but the young woman showed wounds to her arms and legs.
A major dragnet was set up and the young woman identified four youths with police records for sexual assaults from police records.
Police said at least one youth confessed but his lawyers later said he did so under pressure.
The case was thrown into turmoil when it emerged the young woman had, before entering the police, made a similar claim of rape in the past which turned out to be imaginary.
